## [Record 009] 1925 Hampyeong Heungsan Co., Ltd. — Maeil Sinbo Report and Company Registration
URL: https://lsaru23-ai.github.io/hp-db-archive/en/rec-009.html · 네이버 원문: https://blog.naver.com/congcongyi/224480530525

「128년의 기록과 보도」 · 기록 009
**"Historical Records & Media Coverage" presents period newspapers, official gazettes, documents, institutional records and press coverage related to the Lee Dong-beom family of Hampyeong, together with their original text (or, where a source is hard to read, the parts that can be read).**
**Each entry separates what the record confirms from what it cannot confirm on its own.**
**Category** [Primary source] Newspaper report + gazette registration notice
**Record dates** 24 October 1925, *Maeil Sinbo* · 4 December 1925, *Official Gazette of the Government-General of Korea* No. 3988
**Period covered** Cooperative founded 1920 (as reported) → company established 3 Oct. 1925, registered 12 Oct. 1925 (gazette)
**Original** *Maeil Sinbo* page image in series [Part 6](https://lsaru23-ai.github.io/hp-db-archive/en/post6.html); gazette: [Korean History Database, No. 3988 commercial registration](https://db.history.go.kr/modern/gb/level.do?levelId=gb_1925_12_04_a39880_0390)

### About this record

This record shows how the Hampyeong Industrial Cooperative of [Record 008](https://blog.naver.com/congcongyi/224480526816) became a joint-stock company in 1925.

### Original text: "咸平에 有望한 興産株式會社 萬無一失을 自期" (***Maeil Sinbo***, 24 Oct. 1925)

[원면 설명 1] Maeil Sinbo, 24 Oct 1925, excerpt of the original page (Source: Maeil Sinbo)
[원면 설명 2] [Excerpt 1] Opening portion of a “Foundation of a Stock Company” (株式會社設立) notice in the commercial registration section of the Official Gazette of the Government-General of Korea No. 3988, 4 December 1925. Reading right to left: trade name (商號), head office (本店), purpose (目的), capital (資本ノ總額, 80,000 won), par value per share, amount paid in, method of public notice, date of foundation (3 October 1925) and term of existence. This is a cropped excerpt of the original vertical Japanese text; the officers’ “name and address” (氏名住所) column is not included. — Source: Official Gazette of the Government-General of Korea No. 3988, 4 December 1925.
[원면 설명 3] [Excerpt 2] Officers and registration portion of the same notice. Under “Names and addresses of auditors” (監査役ノ氏名住所) appear the names of three auditors, and under “Names and addresses of directors” (取締役ノ氏名住所) those of four directors; to the left are the director to represent the company (會社ヲ代表スヘキ取締役ノ氏名 — one of the directors, listed once more here), the registration date (registered 12 October 1925) and the registry office (Kwangju District Court, Hampyeong Branch Office). All address and lot-number (番地) text attached to the names has been removed so that it is not published. Cropped excerpt of the original vertical Japanese text. — Source: Official Gazette of the Government-General of Korea No. 3988, 4 December 1925.
> 全南咸平郡興産株式會社는大正九年度에該郡有力者李載爀張志文氏外諸氏의發起로
> 興産組合을組織하야今日까지營業을繼續한바意外에好成績을得하야相當한利益을
> 配當한고로一般組合員은一層奮鬪하야資金八萬圓의株式會社로變更하야十月十六日에
> 登記手續까지終了된고로業務를一層擴張하는中이라는데 …
> 營業의目的은精米、繰綿을主로하고更히諸般農産物을取扱한다하며役員은左와如하다더라(木浦)
> 社長兼專務取締役李載爀▲取締役張志文▲同金琮泰▲同申鉉麟(?)▲監査役李亨己▲同李啓攻(?)
> ▲同韓圭興▲相談役李載昇　同金東昕

### Summary translation (the article's account)

Hampyeong Heungsan Co. began as an industrial cooperative founded in 1920 (Taishō 9) at the initiative of Lee Jae-hyeok, Jang Ji-mun and others. Its results were good enough to pay dividends, and it was reorganized as a joint-stock company with capital of 80,000 won, completing registration on 16 October.
Its main business was rice milling and cotton ginning, along with other farm produce. Officers included Lee Jae-hyeok as president and managing director, and Lee Jae-seung as adviser (相談役).

### What the record confirms

According to the *Maeil Sinbo*, the cooperative was founded in 1920 at the initiative of Lee Jae-hyeok and others, and completed registration as a joint-stock company with capital of 80,000 won on 16 October 1925.
The commercial registration page in *Official Gazette* No. 3988 (published 4 Dec. 1925) gives the company's date of establishment as 3 October 1925 and its date of registration as 12 October 1925.
The *Maeil Sinbo* reported registration as "completed on 16 October," which differs from the gazette's registration date (12 October). These two sources alone do not show whether the newspaper referred to a different procedural step or simply reported a different date. This entry gives the gazette's dates as the official registration record and the newspaper's date as contemporary reporting.
According to the *Maeil Sinbo*, Lee Jae-hyeok was president and managing director and Lee Jae-seung was an adviser.
The company's registration appears in the Government-General's *Official Gazette* No. 3988 (published 4 Dec. 1925). The registered officers listed there do not include advisers, so Lee Jae-seung's adviser title is confirmed only by the newspaper (series Part 6).

### What this record alone cannot confirm

The company's actual performance and how long it lasted
What each officer actually did
Why the newspaper's "16 October" differs from the gazette's registration date of 12 October
A full transcription of the gazette registration (this entry gives only the dates of establishment and registration)
The 1920 founding year (currently attested only by the 1925 newspaper report)

### Related posts

Series [Part 6](https://lsaru23-ai.github.io/hp-db-archive/en/post6.html) · [Record 008](https://blog.naver.com/congcongyi/224480526816)
---
Sources**: ***Maeil Sinbo***, 24 October 1925; **[Official Gazette of the Government-General of Korea No. 3988 (4 December 1925), commercial registration](https://db.history.go.kr/modern/gb/level.do?levelId=gb_1925_12_04_a39880_0390), Korean History Database.

## [Record 011] 1938 Dong-A Ilbo — "Chun-gang Lee Jae-seung, Faithful to the Old Ways"
URL: https://lsaru23-ai.github.io/hp-db-archive/en/rec-011.html · 네이버 원문: https://blog.naver.com/congcongyi/224480533565

「128년의 기록과 보도」 · 기록 011
**"Historical Records & Media Coverage" presents period newspapers, official gazettes, documents, institutional records and press coverage related to the Lee Dong-beom family of Hampyeong, together with their original text (or, where a source is hard to read, the parts that can be read).**
**Each entry separates what the record confirms from what it cannot confirm on its own.**
**Category** [Primary source] Newspaper profile
**Record date** 4 October 1938, *Dong-A Ilbo* (Hampyeong feature page)
**Original** Page image in series [Part 6](https://lsaru23-ai.github.io/hp-db-archive/en/post6.html); the newspaper can be viewed through the Dong-A Ilbo archive and Naver News Library

### About this record

A stand-alone profile of Lee Dong-beom's eldest son, Chun-gang Lee Jae-seung, printed with his photograph.
The headline means "Mr. Chun-gang Lee Jae-seung, faithful to the old ways."

### Original text (partial)

[원면 설명 1] Dong-A Ilbo, 4 Oct 1938, excerpt of the original page (Source: Dong-A Ilbo)
> 古道에充實
> 春崗 李載昇氏
> 咸平面長을□하신(?) 明哲한氏는 度量無限하고 用心周到하고 萬事
> 整然하고 正心바로 그것이다. 前年에 氏의 箕山農場小作人組合에
> 自手勞力하야 … (remainder being transcribed)

### Translation (legible part)

Mr. Chun-gang Lee Jae-seung, faithful to the old ways. (A phrase concerning the head of Hampyeong township — reading and meaning uncertain.) He is wise and broad-minded, thorough in his care, orderly in all matters and upright of heart.
Last year (?) he personally lent his efforts to the tenant farmers' union of his Gisan Farm …

### What the record confirms

In October 1938 the *Dong-A Ilbo* featured Lee Jae-seung in a profile of his own on its Hampyeong page.
The headline writes his pen name as 春崗. Some family materials write it 春岡; the two spellings are kept on record separately, and neither is treated as an error.
The article contains the phrase 咸平面長 (head of Hampyeong township) and a passage on the Gisan Farm tenant farmers' union.

### What this record alone cannot confirm

Whether, when and for how long he served as township head (the reading and meaning of the passage around 咸平面長 are uncertain; also left open in series Part 6)
The correct characters of his pen name (春崗 / 春岡)
His role in the tenant farmers' union and what it actually did
The full text of the article (partly transcribed)

## [Record 023] 1877 Seungjeongwon Ilgi — Relief Funds from Lee Hong-gyu, Former Owijang of Hampyeong
URL: https://lsaru23-ai.github.io/hp-db-archive/en/rec-023.html · 네이버 원문: https://blog.naver.com/congcongyi/224483259069

「128년의 기록과 보도」 · 기록 023
**“Historical Records & Media Coverage” presents period newspapers, official gazettes, documents, institutional records and press coverage related to the Lee Dong-beom family of Hampyeong, together with their original text (or, where a source is hard to read, the parts that can be read).**
**Each entry separates what the record confirms from what it cannot confirm on its own.**
**Category** [Primary source] *Seungjeongwon Ilgi* (Royal Secretariat Diary)
**Record date** Gojong 14/8/21 (lunar) = 27 September 1877
**Related entries** Military-examination diploma (*hongpae*), 4th month of 1871 (held by the family) · *Seungjeongwon Ilgi*, Gojong 8 (1871) 9/13 and 9/21; Gojong 20 (1883) 5/3
**Source** National Institute of Korean History, *Seungjeongwon Ilgi* database; original images at Kyujanggak Institute, Seoul National University
**Original** [Entry of Gojong 14/8/21](https://sjw.history.go.kr/id/SJW-K14080210-01700) (page image via the "Kyujanggak original" link)

### About this record

Lee Gye-song (李啓松), father of Seok-am Lee Dong-beom, is also recorded in the *Hampyeong Lee Clan Comprehensive Genealogy* under another name, Hong-gyu (弘奎). The *Seungjeongwon Ilgi* for 1877 lists "Lee Hong-gyu, former *owijang* of Hampyeong" (咸平前五衛將李弘奎) among those who contributed 1,500 *nyang* toward famine relief. The entry is a proposal by the Ministry of Personnel to reward voluntary contributors (願納人), based on the report and roll submitted by Yi Don-sang, Governor of Jeolla Province, on completing the relief.
The Hampyeong head family still holds the royal diploma (*hongpae*) recording Lee Hong-gyu's success in the military examination in 1871.

### Original text (excerpt)

> 各邑願納人中 … 咸平前五衛將李弘奎, 金堤前五衛將金光栢, 各錢一千五百兩,
> 上項二人, 施以相當職調用。

### Translation

Among the voluntary contributors of the counties … Lee Hong-gyu, former *owijang* of Hampyeong, and Kim Gwang-baek, former *owijang* of Gimje, each gave 1,500 *nyang*; it is proposed that these two be employed in suitable posts.

### The military-examination diploma kept by the family

> 敎旨
> 閑良李弘奎武科乙科
> 第二人及第出身者
> 同治十年四月　日

"Royal decree. *Hallyang* Lee Hong-gyu has passed the military examination, second place in the second (*eulgwa*) class, and is admitted to official status. 4th month of the 10th year of Tongzhi (1871)." An accompanying title strip also reads "閑良李弘奎武科乙科第二人." *Hallyang* (閑良) denotes a candidate of military background who had not yet entered office. The genealogy entry for Lee Gye-song (1989 edition, vol. 8, p. 779; online genealogy printout, vol. 11, p. 1080) records "also named Hong-gyu (弘奎)" and a military *cheomchu* title in the *sinmi* year (1871), the same year as the diploma.

### Other entries under the same name (*Seungjeongwon Ilgi*) — given his examination success (4th month of 1871) and the sequence of his career, these entries are likely to refer to the same person (an inference); each entry is still to be checked individually against the examination roster and is not yet confirmed

9/13/1871 (lunar; 26 Oct.): appointed *owijang* (李弘奎爲五衛將); in a later round, listed as sole nominee for *cheomji jungchubusa* (僉知單李弘奎)
9/21/1871 (lunar): *owijang* Lee Hong-gyu and others replaced on grounds of illness
1873–1874: repeated appointments as *owijang* and replacements on grounds of illness
5/3/1883 (lunar; 7 June): named on a list of additional *owijang* appointments (五衛將加設單)

### What the record confirms

A government record shows that "Lee Hong-gyu, former *owijang* of Hampyeong" contributed 1,500 *nyang* to famine relief in 1877. On the original page image, the name, place and amount match the database transcription.
The Ministry of Personnel proposed employing him in a suitable post in recognition.
He had already served as *owijang* before 1877 ("former *owijang*").
Lee Hong-gyu passed the military examination in the 4th month of 1871, second place in the *eulgwa* class (diploma held by the family). The *Seungjeongwon Ilgi* records an *owijang* of the same name appointed in the 9th month of the same year, and the 1877 entry names "Lee Hong-gyu, former *owijang* of Hampyeong." That the examination and the *owijang* appointment belong to the same man's career is an inference from their timing.

### What this record alone cannot confirm

Whether he was **actually appointed** to a post as proposed (the entry records only the proposal)
What 1,500 *nyang* amounted to at the time, or how it was paid
Whether the Lee Hong-gyu of the 1871, 1873 and 1883 entries is the Lee Hong-gyu of Hampyeong; those entries give no place of origin. The grounds for regarding them as likely to refer to the same person are the 1871 examination diploma followed in the same year by an *owijang* appointment (an inference from timing), the 1877 entry ("former *owijang* of Hampyeong"), the genealogy's "also named Hong-gyu" and its 1871 military *cheomchu* title, and the 1913 *Joseon Sinsa Daedongbo* entry for Lee Dong-beom giving his father as "李弘奎 (同中樞)" ([Record 026](https://blog.naver.com/congcongyi/224483254565)).
The exact name of the 1871 examination, his overall rank, and the residence and father's name recorded in the examination roster. These will be added once the roster has been checked.
Whether the posts of *owijang* and *cheomji jungchubusa* involved actual duties or were largely honorary

### Related posts

Series [Special Edition 1](https://lsaru23-ai.github.io/hp-db-archive/en/ex1.html) · [Part 5](https://lsaru23-ai.github.io/hp-db-archive/en/post5.html)

### Sources

*Seungjeongwon Ilgi*, Gojong 14/8/21; Gojong 8/9/13 and 9/21; Gojong 10/1/13 and 12/27; Gojong 11/1/7; Gojong 20/5/3. NIKH *Seungjeongwon Ilgi* database; Kyujanggak Institute originals.

## [Record 024] 1891 Seungjeongwon Ilgi — A Posthumous Title for Filial Piety: Lee Gyeong-heon
URL: https://lsaru23-ai.github.io/hp-db-archive/en/rec-024.html · 네이버 원문: https://blog.naver.com/congcongyi/224483239443

「128년의 기록과 보도」 · 기록 024
**“Historical Records & Media Coverage” presents period newspapers, official gazettes, documents, institutional records and press coverage related to the Lee Dong-beom family of Hampyeong, together with their original text (or, where a source is hard to read, the parts that can be read).**
**Each entry separates what the record confirms from what it cannot confirm on its own.**
**Category** [Primary source] *Seungjeongwon Ilgi*
**Record date** Gojong 27/12/23 (lunar) = 1 February 1891
**Source** NIKH *Seungjeongwon Ilgi* database; original images at Kyujanggak Institute, Seoul National University
**Original** [Entry of Gojong 27/12/23](https://sjw.history.go.kr/id/SJW-K27120230-01600) (page image via the "Kyujanggak original" link)

### About this record

This is the record of a posthumous office granted to Lee Gyeong-heon (李警憲, 1825–1855), grandfather of Seok-am Lee Dong-beom. The *Hampyeong Lee Clan Comprehensive Genealogy* notes "*gyogwan*" (敎官), among other titles, under his name; this government record relates to that entry.

### Original text (excerpt)

> 故學生李警憲, 贈童蒙敎官, 孝行卓異贈職事, 承傳。

### Translation

The late Lee Gyeong-heon, *haksaeng* (a scholar without office), is posthumously appointed *dongmong gyogwan* (instructor of youth); the royal order to grant this posthumous office for his outstanding filial piety is hereby transmitted.

### What the record confirms

In 1891 (12th lunar month of 1890) the court posthumously granted Lee Gyeong-heon the title of *dongmong gyogwan*, for "outstanding filial piety" (孝行卓異).
The record describes him as *haksaeng*, a term for a scholar without office; this record alone does not settle his whole life history.

### What this record alone cannot confirm

Whether the genealogy's "*gyogwan*" refers only to this posthumous title
What his filial conduct consisted of
Who petitioned for the title (it came about 35 years after his death)
The basis for the genealogy's additional entry "*jobong daebu*" (朝奉大夫, a junior fourth-rank grade), or how it relates to the title of *dongmong gyogwan*

### Related posts

Series [Special Edition 1](https://lsaru23-ai.github.io/hp-db-archive/en/ex1.html)
*Seungjeongwon Ilgi*, Gojong 27/12/23. NIKH *Seungjeongwon Ilgi* database; Kyujanggak Institute originals.
*Hampyeong Lee Clan Comprehensive Genealogy* (1989 edition), vol. 8, Hyou-gong branch, p. 779; the same entry appears in the online genealogy printout, vol. 11, p. 1080.

## [Record 026] 1913 Joseon Sinsa Daedongbo — Entries for Lee Dong-beom and His Son Lee Jae-seung
URL: https://lsaru23-ai.github.io/hp-db-archive/en/rec-026.html · 네이버 원문: https://blog.naver.com/congcongyi/224483254565

「128년의 기록과 보도」 · 기록 026
**“Historical Records & Media Coverage” presents period newspapers, official gazettes, documents, institutional records and press coverage related to the Lee Dong-beom family of Hampyeong, together with their original text (or, where a source is hard to read, the parts that can be read).**
**Each entry separates what the record confirms from what it cannot confirm on its own.**
**Category** [Primary source] Biographical directory
**Record date** 1913 (*Joseon Sinsa Daedongbo*, "Comprehensive Register of Korean Gentlemen"; per the database's bibliographic data — original volume not yet examined)
**Source** NIKH Korean History Database, "Modern Biographical Materials" (data from the *Joseon Sinsa Daedongbo*)
**Original** [Lee Dong-beom](https://db.history.go.kr/id/im_108_02446) · [Lee Jae-seung](https://db.history.go.kr/id/im_108_03660) (database transcription; page images of the book not yet obtained)

### About this record

A directory compiling the careers of local notables, published early in the colonial period. It contains separate entries for Lee Dong-beom and his eldest son, Lee Jae-seung. As with most such directories, the information was probably supplied by the subjects or their families.

### Original (database entries, excerpt)

Lee Dong-beom (李東範): clan seat Hampyeong · born 13 Nov. 1869 · father 李弘奎(同中樞) · 縣監 號孝友堂 李慴 十七世孫 · education 漢文受學 · career 肇慶廟參奉 中樞院議官 正三品通政 · assessment 萬頃 殷栗郡守 作宰廉直 蔚有遺愛
Lee Jae-seung (李載昇): clan seat Hampyeong · born 9 Oct. 1890 · father 李東範(通政) · 縣監 號孝友堂 李慴 十八世孫 · education 漢文受學 · career … 咸平郡公立普通學校 學務委員

### Translation

Lee Dong-beom: of the Hampyeong Lee clan, born 13 November 1869; father Lee Hong-gyu (*dongjungchu*); seventeenth-generation descendant of Lee Seup (pen name Hyowudang), a former county magistrate; educated in classical Chinese. Career: *chambong* of Jogyeongmyo, councillor of the Jungchuwon, senior third rank (*tongjeong daebu*). Assessment: "As magistrate of Mangyeong and Eunyul he governed with integrity and left many fond memories."
Lee Jae-seung: of the Hampyeong Lee clan, born 9 October 1890; father Lee Dong-beom (*tongjeong*); eighteenth-generation descendant of Lee Seup; educated in classical Chinese. School affairs commissioner (學務委員) of Hampyeong County Public Common School.

### What the record confirms

Around 1913 Lee Dong-beom and Lee Jae-seung were both listed in a contemporary biographical directory.
Lee Dong-beom's listed career (Jogyeongmyo *chambong*, Jungchuwon councillor, senior third rank) broadly matches the Official Gazette ([Record 001](https://blog.naver.com/congcongyi/224480488919), Record 007).
His father is given as "李弘奎." Together with the genealogy's "Lee Gye-song, also named Hong-gyu," this is a contemporary record supporting that Lee Gye-song and Lee Hong-gyu were the same person ([Record 023](https://blog.naver.com/congcongyi/224483259069)).
Lee Jae-seung served as a school affairs commissioner of Hampyeong County Public Common School.

### What this record alone cannot confirm

The objectivity of the assessment "作宰廉直 蔚有遺愛." It is an **evaluative phrase printed in the directory**, not an independent official performance record; this entry reports only that the phrase appears.
The exact meaning of "同中樞." It appears to abbreviate *dongji jungchubusa* (junior second rank), but this is not confirmed. His gravestone and the genealogy record a *cheomji jungchubusa* (senior third rank) title; whether these reflect different periods needs checking.
The date and circumstances of the promotion to the senior third rank (the gazette record is still being checked)
How long Lee Jae-seung served as commissioner, or what he did

### Related posts

Series [Part 5](https://lsaru23-ai.github.io/hp-db-archive/en/post5.html) · [Part 6](https://lsaru23-ai.github.io/hp-db-archive/en/post6.html)
*Joseon Sinsa Daedongbo* (1913, per database bibliographic data), NIKH Korean History Database, Modern Biographical Materials.

> 앞으로 추가될 기록(1902~1904 관보, 1909년 경찰 기록, 1930년 신문, 『백범일지』, 기관 기록, 언론 보도)은 검증을 마친 뒤 날짜 순서에 맞춰 이 표에 넣습니다. 연표 표시 순서는 자료 일자 기준입니다. 예를 들어 1947년 6월 「光明」은 같은 해 12월 『백범일지』 초판보다 앞에, 2002년 보도는 2003년 조사보고서보다 앞에 놓입니다.
> Further records will be added in date order after verification.

**Lee Dong-beom Family of Hampyeong: A Brief Chronology of Ancestors' Careers and Offices**

(Generations follow the genealogy's generation numbers (世); relationships in brackets are to the author. Sources: [G] government records · [F] originals held by the family · [Gen] *Hampyeong Lee Clan Comprehensive Genealogy* · [L] later compilations and newspapers)

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

The dates for Lee Jae-seung and Lee Sang-rae follow the family register (the genealogy gives their years of death as 1959 and 1969, the latter on the 20th day of the first lunar month).*
